meta.project: Reproduction of Tang et al., 'Deep Graph Reinforcement Learning for UAV-Enabled Multi-User Secure Communications' (IEEE TMC 2025)

architecture.description: Rician fading K=10 dB; LoS = half-wavelength ULA steering vector at the UAV; path loss 30 + 22 log(d) dB; channels returned divided by sigma_0 (noise power = 1) for float32 conditioning.
R_k = log2(1 + |h^H w_k|^2 / (sum_{l!=k} |h^H w_l|^2 + 1)); R_sec = (R_k - R_E,k)^+; power normalisation sqrt(P) * W / ||W||.

K nodes (user + its eavesdropper); D GCN layers; node weights shared; message generation -> max aggregation over the other nodes -> concat -> output MLP; PReLU; embedding e_k updated, channel part kept; final normalisation.
Flattened channels of all K pairs -> all K beamformers; input size tied to K (one MLP per K).
architecture.paper: 'conventional deep model with pure MLP structure'

architecture.description: Unsupervised, loss = -mean sum secrecy rate; fresh random layouts, UAV positions and fading every mini-batch; best-validation checkpoint kept.
Per-instance projected-gradient (Adam) ascent on the sum secrecy rate, multi-start (MRT, ZF, random). Stand-in for [45], which the paper does not describe.
State = UAV position + channel features; action = (dx, dy) in [-1,1]^2 scaled to metres; reward = sum secrecy rate with GNN beamforming at the new position; fresh fading every step.
Stable-Baselines3 SAC (twin critics, target networks, auto-tuned temperature) plus periodic deterministic evaluation that keeps the best policy.

Area centre, geometric centre, circumcentre (minimum enclosing circle), polygon centroid (convex hull); exhaustive grid search of the expected secrecy rate, scored with GNN beamforming (problem (23)-(25), constraint (24)).

changes.title: Project scaffold, typed YAML configuration, run directories
changes.after: Package src/uavsec, configs/default.yaml as the single source of truth (Table I + clearly marked assumptions), every run writes config.yaml, log.txt, metrics.json with git hash, seed and wall time.
changes.reason: Traceability: every number in the report must come from a recorded run.
changes.evidence: 19 unit tests (rates vs numpy reference, permutation equivariance, power constraint, env, heuristics).

changes.title: Initial model choices where the paper is silent
changes.after: GNN hidden width 128, weights shared across nodes, max aggregation, PReLU; MLP 3x512; OPT 16 restarts x 500 iterations; SAC episode length 100, max step 5 m, networks 2x256; area-centre start; eavesdropper 20 m from its user at a random bearing.
changes.reason: Paper gives no widths, episode length, step size or OPT details.
changes.evidence: Local CPU sanity check: GNN 12.6 vs MLP 6.4 bps/Hz at a 30 dB lower SNR (30 epochs).

changes.title: PReLU on the last axis
changes.before: torch nn.PReLU(num_parameters) on tensors shaped (B, K, H) -> shape mismatch error.
changes.after: FeaturePReLU: one learnable slope per feature on the last axis.
changes.reason: Bug found by the first tests.

changes.title: Server environment: torch pinned, CUDA check
changes.before: Upgrading stable-baselines3 silently replaced torch 2.5.1+cu121 by torch 2.14 (CUDA 13); driver 535 (CUDA 12.2) cannot run it, so training fell back to CPU.
changes.after: torch==2.5.1 pinned in the same pip command; run_all.sh aborts if CUDA is not available; concurrent runs no longer reinstall the package.
changes.reason: GPU 2 showed 0% utilisation while the process used 2700% CPU.

changes.title: Gradient-norm clipping (1.0) for beamformer training
changes.reason: GNN reached 17.3 bps/Hz and then collapsed to about 5 near epoch 125.
changes.evidence: Clipped runs stay stable for all 300 epochs (about 18 bps/Hz at 128 width).

changes.title: Hypothesis A: noise power 30 dB higher (configs/paper_snr.yaml)
changes.before: Table I as printed gives a per-antenna SNR of about 55 dB; zero-forcing alone reaches 86-90 bps/Hz at K=8, far above the paper's OPT curve (about 15-18).
changes.after: Re-run everything with noise 1.2e-10 W (a W/mW slip).
changes.reason: Paper's Fig. 9b looks consistent with an SNR about 30 dB lower.
changes.evidence: At 1 W, K=8: GNN 20.8 / OPT 35.1 / MLP 12.4 (GNN = 59% of OPT). But the deployment optimum was still 24 m off and the rate map stayed flat, so this hypothesis does not explain Fig. 7/8. Dropped as the main profile after the user pointed out that 30+22log(d) is the official formula.
changes.impact_on_results: Kept only as an extra reference (configs/paper_snr.yaml).

changes.title: Fixed SAC layout digitised from Fig. 7
changes.after: configs/layouts/paper_fig7.yaml: 8 users + 8 eavesdroppers read off the figure (+-1 m), including the user hidden behind the legend at (137, 143); UAV starts at (100, 100). Paper reference optimum (56, 140) and Fig. 8 bar heights stored in the same file for comparison only.
changes.reason: Needed to compare the learned deployment with the paper's.
changes.evidence: User approved the layout figure (outputs/layout/layout_check.png). Pairing of eavesdroppers to users is an inference (paper does not say). A test of both pairings of the U5/U6 cluster could not tell them apart, so the one closest to 'about 20 m' was kept.

changes.title: Channel interpretation: natural log + horizontal distance (configs/calibrated.yaml)
changes.before: log10 and 3-D distance in the path loss (the 'standard' reading). Deployment optimum 45-62 m from the paper's (56, 140); heuristics reach over 90% of the optimum (paper Fig. 8: 39-61%); rate map almost flat.
changes.after: system.path_loss_log = ln, system.distance_model = horizontal, system.array_axis = x. All Table I numbers unchanged.
changes.reason: The paper writes 'log(d)' without base and does not say which distance. A sensitivity study over 8 combinations (log base x distance x ULA axis, plus noise levels) found the combination that reproduces three independent paper results at once: Fig. 7 optimum location, Fig. 8 heuristic/optimum profile, secrecy-rate level.
changes.evidence: OPT beamformer, optimum distance to paper: ln+3D+x 10 m, ln+horizontal+x 17 m, ln+horizontal+y 25 m, log10 variants 44-62 m. Fig. 8 profile error: ln+horizontal+x 0.15 (best), log10 variants 0.42-0.48. Rate level 30 bps/Hz vs paper 23. Chosen by the user after reviewing the study (scripts/study_deployment_sensitivity.py, report section 5).
changes.impact_on_results: Main profile. Table I as printed is kept as a reference run.

changes.title: Exhaustive search for the Fig. 7 optimum uses the GNN
changes.before: First changed to the OPT beamformer (joint optimum of (7)-(9)).
changes.after: Default eval.search_beamformer = gnn (problem (23)-(25) fixes W = GNN output, eq. (24)); the OPT-based optimum is always computed and reported next to it.
changes.reason: User challenged whether the code still follows the paper; constraint (24) requires GNN beamforming inside the deployment problem.
changes.evidence: Consequence: the optimum now depends on GNN quality, which led to C10.

changes.title: GNN capacity: hidden 128 -> 256, batches per epoch 20 -> 50
changes.before: hidden 128, 20 mini-batches per epoch: GNN reaches 71% of OPT on the calibrated model; its rate map put the optimum 45 m from the paper's.
changes.reason: Better GNN -> rate map closer to the true one. Architecture, loss, lr 0.005, 300 epochs, batch 512 unchanged.
changes.evidence: 128/20: 71% of OPT, optimum 45 m off. 256/20: 74%, 8 m. 128/50: 75%, 9 m. 256/50: 76%, 0 m. Three independent seeds at 256/50 (script study_gnn_optimum.py): 2.8 m, 2.8 m, 80 m (the third is a weaker GNN and is never selected because the deployed GNN is the best-validation seed).
changes.impact_on_results: Training time 3 min -> 11 min per seed on GPU. Superseded by C16 (hidden 512 + cosine).

changes.title: Log-compressed channel magnitude as GNN input
changes.reason: Channel gain spans decades under the horizontal-distance path loss (feature 99th percentile about 67, median 1.8).
changes.evidence: No gain: linear GNN 8.93 / MLP 6.78 vs log GNN 8.90 / MLP 6.63 bps/Hz (100 epochs). Re-tested on 2026-10-14 in the dense user cluster (G8: 512 + log -> 5.6 val, broken; G9: 256 + log -> 73% of OPT, same as linear). Not adopted.

changes.title: SAC: log-compressed state, reward scale 0.1, keep the best evaluated policy
changes.before: Linear state, raw reward (about 14-28), last policy kept. SAC reached about 18 bps/Hz in the first 100 episodes and then degraded; final point (121, 118) was 63% of the optimum and 20% below the best heuristic.
changes.after: sac.obs_transform = log, sac.reward_scale = 0.1 (training only; logs and figures use the unscaled R_sec), sac.eval_every_episodes = 10 with the best deterministic policy restored at the end. Extended by C17.
changes.reason: Large channel features and reward scale hurt the critics; SAC's last iterate is noisy.
changes.evidence: Calibrated: final point (73.6, 154.5), 92.8% of the optimum, +17% over the best heuristic. Table I: 93.1%, +4.8%.

changes.title: Smaller fixes
changes.before: latest_run('deployment') also matched 'deployment_sensitivity_*'; '--set' given twice kept only the last list; report crashed when metrics lacked a field.
changes.after: Exact timestamp match; --set accumulates; report tolerates older metrics.

changes.title: Diagnosis: the GNN-based optimum jumped onto spikes right above single users
changes.before: Better GNNs (cosine LR, more width or data) reached 77-80% of OPT but put the Fig. 7 optimum right above user U2 (136, 144) or U1 (88, 158), 37-80 m from the paper's.
changes.after: Both candidates measured with 2048 fading draws: under OPT the paper's cluster (29.3 bps/Hz) beats the point above U2 (25.5); the GNNs reached 101-106% of OPT above U2 but only 70-77% in the cluster.
changes.reason: Find out whether the paper's optimum or the spike is the true optimum.
changes.evidence: Root cause: with the horizontal-distance path loss clamped at 1 m, a UAV right above a user gives that user about 99 dB SNR (impossible at 100 m altitude). The paper's optimum is 21 m from the nearest user, so its model has no such spikes.

changes.title: Minimum horizontal path-loss distance of 20 m (calibrated profile)
changes.reason: Do not extrapolate the empirical 30 + 22 ln(d) model below 20 m horizontal distance (the paper's user-eavesdropper scale); this removes the unphysical spikes.
changes.evidence: OPT, 2 m grid: 1 m -> optimum 18 m from paper, profile error 0.15; 10 m -> same; 20 m -> 16 m, paper point 96% of max, profile 0.16, rate 29.9; 50 m -> 33 m; 100 m -> 37 m. GNN (256, cosine) at 20 m: 3 seeds give 81-82% of OPT and optima 7.2 / 8.2 / 10.8 m from the paper's.

changes.title: GNN: hidden 512 and cosine learning-rate schedule starting at 0.005
changes.after: gnn.hidden_dim = 512, gnn.lr_schedule = cosine (starts at the Table I value 0.005, decays to 1%). Still 5 GCN layers, batch 512, 300 episodes.
changes.reason: Constant lr plateaued at about 72% of OPT whatever the width or data; the paper gives no schedule. The user approved the schedule on 2026-10-14.
changes.evidence: Constant lr: 256 -> 72%, 512 -> similar (G6), 256 + near-user sampling -> 71% (G10). Cosine: 256 -> 77-82%, 512 -> 80-84%. Hidden 1024 collapsed at lr 0.005 (all secrecy rates clamped to 0, zero gradient). Final candidate 512 + cosine + 20 m: 84% of OPT, optimum exactly at (56, 140).

changes.title: SAC: 2 gradient steps per step, 2.5 m steps, 175 steps per episode, 3-episode evaluation
changes.before: 1 gradient step, 5 m steps, 100 steps per episode, 1 evaluation episode: SAC stopped 20 m from the optimum and jittered about 5 m per step.
changes.after: sac.gradient_steps = 2, sac.max_step_m = 2.5, sac.episode_length = 175, sac.eval_episodes = 3. Table I SAC values (lr, 500 episodes, mini-batch 64, buffer 1e6, discount 0.99) unchanged.
changes.reason: More updates per sample, smaller steps for a smoother path, horizon long enough to reach the optimum. Fig. 6 of the paper (episode reward about 4.4e3 at about 25 bps/Hz) implies about 170-180 steps per episode.
changes.evidence: With the previous GNN: S1 (2 grad steps) 10.5 m from paper; S3 (+3-episode eval) 5.6 m; S2 (T=200) 13.4 m; S4 (2.5 m, T=200, 1 grad step) 56.9 m; S5 (2.5 m, T=100) 57.7 m (cannot reach); S6 (2 grad steps, 2.5 m, T=175) 3.9 m with 1.0 m jitter.

changes.title: Training UAV positions sampled near users (50%)
changes.before: UAV uniform in the area during GNN training.
changes.reason: Hypothesis: the GNN is weak where SAC places the UAV.
changes.evidence: G10 (constant lr) 71% of OPT; G12/G13 (cosine) 77-79% with optima on the spike above U1 (37 m). No gain over uniform sampling.

changes.title: Memory-efficient max aggregation
changes.before: The max over the other nodes built a B x K x K x H tensor (2 GB for 32k samples): out of memory on the shared GPU.
changes.after: Top-2 trick, O(K) memory, bit-identical results (checked for K = 1, 2, 5, 12 and ties); evaluation chunks of 8192.
changes.reason: Two SAC runs crashed in the final grid search.
changes.evidence: Tests pass; outputs identical to the K x K reference.

open_issues: GNN reaches 82-89% of our OPT across K (85% at K=8); the paper reports its GNN close to its OPT. In absolute terms our OPT matches the paper's OPT closely (Fig. 9a/9b), our GNN is about 10% below the paper's GNN.
GNN trained at 1 W loses ground at 40 dBm (69% of OPT); the paper's GNN keeps closer to OPT there.
Fig. 8: heuristics reach 61-69% of the optimum here vs 39-61% in the paper (same ordering, smaller gaps).
One of three GNN seeds trains worse (validation std 1.57); the deployed GNN is the best-validation seed.
GNN-based optimum per seed: 0.0, 11.7 and 7.2 m from the paper's optimum.
Eavesdropper-to-user pairing in the Fig. 7 layout is inferred; one cluster (U5/U6, E5/E6) is ambiguous.
Only one SAC training seed per profile.
Table I reference profile (log10, 3-D distance) stays unstable and far from the paper's figures, as expected.
